cells.tense: You're here with both hands on it, tending what you decided is worth tending.
cells.ask: Let one finished thing be seen by someone who'd notice, instead of letting it go quietly. What that gives you is permission to put the next one down cleanly.
cells.core:
This part of you can feel which thing matters before it can argue for it, and that feel is working. You've been giving your care where it belongs — two demands pulling in different directions, and you holding both without dropping either. Not by force. By steady attention. You water what's in the ground, your care doesn't exhaust you because it isn't gripping, and what you cultivate comes up rooted. That's what this looks like when it's whole.

The tending has been right. What's left is letting one finished thing be witnessed instead of slipping out the side door. Surrender isn't the same as giving up. It's the release that completion was always going to bring, and it's yours to take now.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending what matters, and you know why you chose it.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: in the part of you that knows what deserves your attention before you can explain why

cells.tense: You're already standing in a harvest that hasn't grown yet, bracing for a moment that can't be scheduled.
cells.ask: Name one thing that's already fully imagined, and let yourself feel satisfied in it before asking it to become more. What that gives you is satisfaction that doesn't need managing.
cells.core:
When this part is going well, you tend at the speed of the thing growing. You water what's in the ground and wait for it. Your care doesn't exhaust you because it isn't gripping — you're holding space, not clutching at it, and the growing does its own work underneath your hands.

Right now you're tending toward a picture ahead of where the growing is. Watering before the seed is in, correcting before there's a shape to correct, answerable to a future that hasn't arrived. What settles you isn't more tending. It's letting one thing you've already imagined be enough as imagined — felt through rather than converted.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending a version of things that hasn't happened yet.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: in the part of you that knows what deserves your attention before you can explain why

cells.tense: You knew what mattered and you set the care down, and you're still standing where you set it down.
cells.ask: Take one small thing you'd already decided was worth your care, and do the next single piece of tending for it — not because you feel ready, but because it descends from something you once chose. What that gives you is your own shine, earned rather than mustered.
cells.core:
When this part is going well, the knowing turns straight into tending, no gap in between. You see what matters and your hands are already on it. The care moves through you without needing to be talked into itself, and you finish what you start.

The seeing is still yours. You can still feel which thing it was. What stopped was the tending, and enough distance has built up that starting again feels like an argument with yourself. Pushing at the seeing won't help; the seeing was never the missing piece. Pick up one thing whose worth you already decided, at the size of a single hour, and let the doing draw the current back through.
cells.sheetLine: You know what mattered. You stopped tending it.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: in the part of you that knows what deserves your attention before you can explain why

cells.tense: The choosing is already happening through you, and it gets described as something that just happened on its own.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, that you're the one tending this — not the situation, not the circumstances. What that gives you is release from carrying it as though it were happening to you.
cells.core:
When this part is going well, you know your own hand in it. You can point to the thing you chose to protect, the thing you chose to let run out, and call the choosing yours. That recognition is quiet, and it holds the whole thing together.

That choosing is running daily and it's shaping things, but the credit has drifted off it. The situation gets described as doing the tending, with you just there for it. Take back the simpler, truer description: this is yours, and you've been carrying it. Letting that be seen — by you, then by someone else — is the release that finishing was supposed to give.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one tending it. You haven't said so.
